My dog has always had a habit of eating things she absolutely should not.
But until that one Saturday, socks and the occasional tissue had been about as bad as it got.
I was folding laundry, only half paying attention.
When I turned back around, one sock was there and the other one had completely vanished.
There was no trace of where it had gone.
At first I figured it had just gotten mixed into a pile somewhere.
But she was sitting there looking a little too pleased with herself, tail wagging, giving off serious guilty-dog energy from across the room.
I checked under the couch, behind the laundry basket, even in the hallway closet.
I was genuinely convinced the sock had just rolled off somewhere.
For a good ten minutes I refused to consider the much more obvious explanation sitting right in front of me.
A few hours later, she started acting off.
She wasn't eating her dinner.
She was just lying around looking miserable, and that's when I actually put it together and realized where that missing sock had probably ended up.
I called the emergency vet, feeling slightly ridiculous explaining the situation over the phone.
But they didn't seem surprised at all.
Honestly, that told me this happens a lot more often than I would have guessed.
We rushed over.
After an X-ray and a lot of anxious waiting in a small room, the vet confirmed it.
There was definitely a sock-shaped object sitting exactly where it shouldn't be.
She showed me the actual image on her screen and pointed to a strange gray blob.
Honestly, it was a relief to finally know what was wrong.
It was also a little unsettling to see actual evidence of my sock sitting inside my own dog.
They gave her something to help her throw it up instead of doing surgery, which was a relief.
Watching the whole process happen in a small vet office was, I guess, not exactly pleasant for either of us.
The vet tech stayed calm through the whole thing and talked softly to my dog the entire time.
I mostly just stood in the corner, trying not to look as squeamish as I actually felt.
Twenty uncomfortable minutes later, the sock reappeared, slightly worse for wear.
My dog immediately looked about ten times better and wagged her tail again, like the whole ordeal had just been a minor inconvenience.
I paid a bill that made me wince a little.
I drove home with a very tired, very hungry dog, and now I keep every single sock in a drawer with an actual latch, just to be safe.
My roommate still brings it up occasionally, usually right before laundry day.
